newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate lower, baht firms late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate lower, baht firms late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 10.75-11.00 percent in late trade on Monday from 11.00-11.50 earlier as dollar selling for baht helped increase market liquidity, dealers said.
"If there was no selling of the dollar for baht in the market today, the interbank rate would have risen further," said one dealer at a U.S. bank.
Dealers said some demand for funds to meet the coming value added tax (VAT) payment stemmed the interbank rate from falling further. The VAT must be paid in the middle of every month.
The baht strengthened to 25.630-25.635 to the dollar late from 25.635-25.640 early on dollar selling, dealers said.
"There was more dollar selling than buying today. Most of the dollar selling was from Singapore," said another dealer at a European bank.
Dealers said players were selling dollars for baht due to the tightening money supply and the relatively high baht interest rates.
The bid/offer range for the one-month dollar/baht swap premium was at 9.00/10.00 satangs per dollar late, unchanged from early morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.65, unchanged from Friday.
